interactions.summary: Jiang keeps the room on the same question, nudging a student toward the idea that absolute will is God-like, then pulling out the answer that human connection to God happens through love.
A student offers the strongest synthesis so far: absolute will is active, finds a path, and creates its own conditions, while contingent will reacts inside material limits.
Jiang says several answers are converging but still asks for the simplest distinction; another student proposes faith versus belief, with only belief needing justification.

claims.claim: Jiang steers the class toward a theological reading in which absolute will is bound up with God, and human access to that alignment happens through love.
The student synthesis Jiang affirms defines absolute will as active and world-making, because it finds or creates the path it needs, while contingent will stays reactive inside material constraints.
claims.temporal_scope: Student formulation endorsed by Jiang on 2026-06-15.

claims.claim: Another classroom simplification proposes that absolute will resembles faith while contingent will resembles belief, because belief still asks for justification whereas faith does not.

signature_moments.moment: The packet's cleanest formulation says absolute will does not wait for conditions; it finds a way and creates the conditions it needs.
signature_moments.source_phrase: it creates its own condition for it is unstoppable
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It anticipates Jiang's later insistence that real will is active rather than merely reactive to the world.

signature_moments.moment: A student snaps the distinction into faith versus belief, with one needing no proof and the other still asking for reasons.
signature_moments.source_phrase: one needs justification. The other doesn't
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It is the packet's sharpest minimalist contrast and a useful compression of the room's search for simpler language.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: A student's shorthand for absolute will because it does not require external justification.
A student's shorthand for contingent will because it still seeks justification from conditions or reasons.

chronology_notes.note: This June 15 packet tightens the exploratory classroom definitions by linking absolute will to God and love, then sharpening it into active, condition-creating faith over reactive belief.
